=============================================================================
1. POSITIONING
=============================================================================
Architect. Prove. Ship. Watch. We ship software.

APSW Labs combines Principal-led system architecture and deterministic AI pipelines with elastic
partner engineering capacity, taking a client from a 10-day architectural blueprint to a full-scale
production platform. It is led by Piotr Solarz-Wnęk, Principal Software Architect with 19+ years
designing mission-critical platforms across institutional finance, industrial IoT and enterprise
SaaS, and creator of Indaba and Gridwright.

APSW Labs is a product and turnkey engineering studio. It does not sell hours, seats in a standup
or body leasing. Clients talk to the architect, not to an account manager.

=============================================================================
2. DELIVERY MODEL: PRINCIPAL-LED, ELASTIC CAPACITY
=============================================================================
Principal architecture at the root. Elastic engineering squads at scale.

- Phase 01, Principal Wedge & Blueprint (APSW Labs core): the Principal Architect personally
  defines C4 boundaries, domain contracts, security isolation and the repository CI guardrails in
  workflow.ai.yml.
- Phase 02, Autonomous Core Synthesis (APSW Labs engine): high-leverage core modules, data
  pipelines and MVPs are synthesized and verified with @indaba/engine and multi-agent councils.
- Phase 03, Elastic Partner Scale-Out (software house squads): for 4-8 engineers of
  long-term feature expansion, mobile apps or a 24/7 SLA, vetted partner squads plug into the
  pre-configured workflow.ai.yml repository. Automated CI gates govern every commit after handoff.

=============================================================================
3. ENGAGEMENT TRACKS
=============================================================================
High-velocity lab sprints (direct APSW Labs Principal execution):
- Track 01, 10-Day Architecture & AI Readiness Blueprint (entry wedge, fixed scope): deep-dive
  codebase and microservice audit, C4 target blueprints, security and isolation review, and an
  executable workflow.ai.yml roadmap.
- Track 02, Turnkey Core MVP / Module Sprint (APSW Labs delivery, 3-6 weeks): fixed-scope delivery
  of a complete MVP, a high-load telemetry backend or a 10M-row Gridwright Pro interface, with over
  90% automated contract tests and Docker / Cloud IaC.
- Track 03, Deterministic AI Factory Setup (in-house team enablement, 2-3 weeks): the engineering
  standard behind Gridwright installed into the client's repository: custom workflow.ai.yml tracks,
  multi-agent review councils, CI drift guards and senior engineering playbooks.

Scaled partner delivery (Principal architecture plus software house squad):
- Track 04, Full-Scale Platform & Dedicated Squads: end-to-end enterprise product development,
  legacy modernization or dedicated multi-disciplinary squads (Java 21, Symfony 8, React,
  Cloud / Data). Architected and gated by APSW Labs, scaled and staffed by vetted partner squads.

Reference build: Idumela, APSW's own B2B reputation engine. It monitors a
brand's reviews, drafts replies in the brand's voice and publishes only after a manager approves.
Multi-tenant (Symfony 8 + React / MUI, tenant isolation, token-credit ledger), built in 2 weeks,
agent-written from specifications behind pre-commit quality gates. Proprietary B2B SaaS built and operated by APSW Labs.

=============================================================================
4. APSW LABS: OPEN-SOURCE PRODUCTS
=============================================================================
Gridwright and Indaba are both MIT licensed.

A. GRIDWRIGHT (apsw-gridwright) - https://apswlabs.com/#gridwright
Gridwright is a React data grid published on npm under the MIT licence, built on a headless,
framework-agnostic engine. Latest release: 0.24.0. Covered by 1,300+ automated tests.

- One pipeline for local and remote data: a data source declares which parts of the query it
  resolved (sort, filter, search, paginate) and the grid applies the rest in memory. Swapping
  `data` for `dataSource` is a one-line change; columns and add-ons stay the same.
- Real table semantics: a <table> with role="grid", aria-sort on the header, one live region, and
  an opt-in wcag() add-on for WCAG 2.2 AA sizing and colours.
- Every feature is an add-on: search, column filters, tree data, grouping with aggregates, export
  (CSV, Excel, Markdown, print, PDF), row and column virtualization (up to ten million rows),
  column layout, inline editing, row detail, cell navigation, responsive layout, URL sync, density,
  loading indicators, row actions.
- Zero runtime dependencies, about 22 kB gzipped for the component, React 18 and 19, TypeScript,
  ESM and CommonJS, translations for en, de, es, fr and pl. Companion package apsw-gridwright-mui
  takes colours, type and dark mode from an MUI theme.
- Never invents a total: when an API sends no count, the grid reports "of many".
- Not included: pivot tables, built-in charts, range selection.
- Licensing: the grid and every add-on are free (MIT). A Pro tier (additional add-ons, priority
  support, migration help) is planned and not priced yet.
- Links: https://www.npmjs.com/package/apsw-gridwright | https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-gridwright |
  https://yaotzin1.github.io/apsw-gridwright/examples/playground/index.html

B. INDABA - https://apswlabs.com/#indaba
Indaba is an open-source, deterministic orchestration, debate and observability engine for AI
agents, written in TypeScript for Node 22 and newer, running on Windows, macOS and Linux. The name
is Zulu for a gathering convened to resolve a hard matter by reaching consensus.
- Status: preview. Newest published version 0.1.0-alpha.5 (`npx indaba@next`); the API is not
  stable below 1.0.
- Deterministic pipelines: a workflow file is a DAG of steps with quality gates, filesystem guards
  and artifact handoffs; the engine, not a model, decides what runs next. Verification is plain
  commands whose exit codes decide pass or fail; a failed step is retried with only the last failure.
- Multi-agent cross-examination: roles backed by different engines (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini,
  Cursor, Antigravity, models over OpenRouter) review each other through a blackboard with a
  consensus arbiter, quorum rules and ping-pong detection.
- Isolation: implementation steps run in an ephemeral git worktree and leave as a patch artifact.
- Observability: every task is a trace; steps and LLM or tool calls are spans with OpenTelemetry
  GenAI attributes, token counts and USD cost where known. Terminal dashboard and local web view.
- Packages: indaba (CLI), @indaba/core, @indaba/engine, @indaba/runners, optional @indaba/tui and
  @indaba/server.
- Links: https://yaotzin1.github.io/indaba/ | https://github.com/yaotzin1/indaba

C. DELIVERY ASSURANCE (https://apswlabs.com/#assurance): Gridwright is built by one architect with the
Indaba engine and coding agents under a single workflow.ai.yml that outranks every other
instruction. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and skill pointers are generated from it; each rule is
marked enforced (a hook, CI job, lint rule or test fails) or guidance; every commit declares its
track (feature, fix, chore, release) and the trailer is checked against the diff; verification
covers smoke tests of the built package, a packaging audit and a security audit. The repository
carries over 1,300 automated tests. APSW brings the same setup to client teams.
